children: shares fell 2.96% in premarket trading after the homebuilder reported fiscal third-quarter revenue down 20% year-over-year to $1.30 billion, with diluted earnings per share of $1.05, down from $1.61 a year earlier. Homes delivered fell 19% to 2,732, and the housing gross profit margin narrowed to 16.5% from 18.2%, which the company attributed to continued pricing pressure, higher relative land costs, and reduced operating leverage. Executive Chairman Jeffrey Mezger said conditions had been "weakening since our June earnings report," with higher mortgage rates pressuring affordability.

Ending backlog rose for the first time in four years, up 2% to 4,398 homes and up 3% in value to $2.05 billion, and the average community count grew 8% to 279. Net orders still fell 12% and monthly orders per community slipped to 3.1 from 3.8. The company repurchased $50 million of stock in the quarter.

KB Home held its full-year guidance, projecting 10,500 to 11,000 deliveries and housing revenue of $4.90 billion to $5.10 billion. For the fourth quarter, the company expects to deliver 3,000 to 3,500 homes.

title: KB Home Stock Slips as Housing Market Weakens
